question: Which prophet of the great drought am I?
reference: 1 Kings 17-19; 2 Kings 2 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Elijah')

clues: I served during the reign of a king whose wife pushed Baal worship hard.
I announced a drought that lasted about three and a half years.
I was fed by ravens, then by a widow whose flour and oil never ran out.
I never died — I was taken up in a windstorm with a fiery chariot.

question: Which reluctant prophet am I?
reference: Jonah 1-4 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Jonah', p. 98)

clues: God sent me to preach to a great enemy city, but I ran the other way.
I boarded a ship at Joppa heading for Tarshish.
A storm hit, and I told the sailors to throw me overboard.
A great fish swallowed me, and I was inside it three days and three nights.

question: Which wise king am I?
reference: 1 Kings 3-11 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Solomon')

clues: When God offered me anything, I asked for wisdom to judge the people.
I settled a dispute between two women over a baby by calling for a sword.
I built the first temple in Jerusalem.
The queen of Sheba traveled far to test me with hard questions.

question: Which strong judge am I?
reference: Judges 13-16 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Samson')

clues: An angel told my parents I would be a Nazirite from birth.
I killed a lion with my bare hands and later found honey in its carcass.
I struck down a thousand men with the jawbone of a donkey.
My strength left me when Delilah had my hair cut.

question: Which faithful widow am I?
reference: Ruth 1-4 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Ruth')

clues: I was a foreigner from Moab who married into an Israelite family.
After my husband died, I refused to leave my mother-in-law.
I gleaned in the fields of a wealthy relative during the barley harvest.
That relative, Boaz, redeemed me, and I became an ancestor of King David.

question: Which outspoken apostle am I?
reference: Matthew 14-16; John 21; Acts 2 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Peter', p. 618)

clues: I was a fisherman from Bethsaida before Jesus called me.
I briefly walked on water toward Jesus before my nerve failed.
I denied knowing Jesus three times on the night of his arrest.
I preached the sermon at Pentecost when about 3,000 were baptized.

question: Which walled city am I?
reference: Joshua 6 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Jericho', p. 34)

clues: I was the first city Israel captured after crossing the Jordan.
I was known for palm trees and springs, and called the city of palms.
Israel's army marched around me once a day for six days.
On the seventh day they circled me seven times, shouted, and my walls collapsed.

question: Which prophet in a foreign court am I?
reference: Daniel 1-6 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Daniel')

clues: I was taken to Babylon as a young man and trained for the king's court.
I refused the king's rich food and asked for vegetables and water instead.
I interpreted a dream about a great image made of different metals.
I was thrown into a den of lions for praying, and came out unharmed.

question: Which reforming king of Judah am I?
reference: 2 Kings 18-20 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Hezekiah')

clues: I removed the high places and even broke up the copper serpent Moses had made.
The Assyrian king Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem in my reign.
An angel struck down 185,000 in the Assyrian camp in one night.
When I was told I would die, I prayed and was given fifteen more years.

question: Which mountain am I?
reference: Exodus 19-20 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Sinai', p. 972)

clues: Moses first met God at me, at a bush that burned but was not consumed.
Israel camped at my base for about a year during the wilderness journey.
I was wrapped in smoke and fire, and the people were told not to touch me.
Moses received the Ten Commandments on me, written on stone tablets.

question: Which man of faith am I?
reference: Genesis 6-9 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Noah')

clues: I lived in a violent world and was told a global judgment was coming.
I built a huge wooden vessel exactly to the dimensions I was given.
I took my family and pairs of every kind of animal aboard.
After the waters dried up, I saw a rainbow set as a sign of a covenant.

question: Which apostle who wanted proof am I?
reference: John 11; 14; 20 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Thomas', p. 1095)

clues: My name is also given as Didymus, meaning twin.
When Jesus decided to go to Bethany near danger, I said we should go and die with him.
I asked Jesus how we could know the way to where he was going.
I said I would not believe he was raised unless I touched his wounds myself.

question: Which leader of Israel am I?
reference: Numbers 13-14; Joshua 1-10 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Joshua', p. 114)

clues: I was one of the twelve sent to spy out the Promised Land.
Only Caleb and I brought back a report urging the people to go in.
I took over leadership of Israel after Moses died.
During a battle at Gibeon, I commanded the sun to stand still.

question: Which successor prophet am I?
reference: 1 Kings 19; 2 Kings 2-13 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Elisha')

clues: I was plowing with twelve pairs of oxen when a prophet threw his cloak over me.
I asked my mentor for a double portion of his spirit as he was taken away.
I purified a spring of bad water by throwing salt into it.
I told the Syrian commander Naaman to wash seven times in the Jordan.

question: Which queen of Persia am I?
reference: Esther 2-9 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Esther')

clues: I was an orphan raised by my older cousin Mordecai.
I was chosen as queen by a Persian king, and I kept my nationality secret.
I approached the king unsummoned, risking death, and invited him to a banquet.
I exposed a plot to destroy my people, and the schemer Haman was hanged.

question: Which small town am I?
reference: Ruth 1; 1 Samuel 16; Micah 5:2; Luke 2 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Bethlehem')

clues: My name means house of bread, and I sat in the territory of Judah.
Ruth and Naomi settled here, and Boaz's fields were nearby.
Samuel came here to anoint the youngest son of Jesse as king.
A prophecy said the ruler of Israel would come out of me, and Jesus was born here.
